'education-num' is one of the strongest predictors, as higher education levels correlate significantly with higher income. 'age' also shows a positive correlation, as older individuals tend to have more work experience and higher earnings. 'workclass' reflects the employment type, with private sector workers often earning more than government or self-employed. 'hours-per-week' is associated with higher income, as those working longer hours tend to earn more. 'sex' has been shown in empirical analyses to correlate with income, though this is debated due to socio-economic factors. Among the current values, these features are most directly linked to income prediction. While 'race' and 'marital-status' have some context, their predictive power is generally weaker and less consistently shown in statistical models compared to the above. The model's prediction of ≤50K is consistent with lower educational attainment, younger age, and moderate work hours, which aligns with these features.
